content.text:
The security scan now reports 0 findings, down from 12. `recon_qa` passes with no journey failures or new divergences, and `run_tests` passes. `go build ./...` is clean. `go vet` shows no problems. Package tests under `modules/markup`, `modules/packages` and `routers/api/packages` also pass.

I did not run the full Go test suite, and I didn't run the Debian integration test (`tests/integration/api_packages_debian_test.go`). It only vets cleanly after the import change.

- **Go dependencies:**
  - I bumped chi to 5.4.0, `golang.org/x/net` to 0.62.0, `klauspost/compress` to 1.20.2 and `golang.org/x/crypto` to the fixed pseudo-version `0.58.1-0.20261009181718-2f1f834330b2`.
  - `go get` also pulled `x/sync`, `x/sys`, `x/text` and `x/tools` up one minor version each.
- **vite:** I bumped it from 8.3.0 to 8.3.3 in `package.json` and regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`. The lockfile diff is about 250 lines, which is more than a single bump would suggest, and I didn't check what else changed.
- **`blakesmith/ar`:**
  - This has no fixed release, and it panics on a negative member size in an uploaded `.deb` file.
  - I replaced it with a small in-tree package, `modules/packages/ar`. It rejects malformed headers with errors instead of panicking.
  - It has a round-trip test and a malformed-input test. `modules/packages/debian` and the Debian tests now use it, and `go mod tidy` dropped the old dependency.
